newsitem.title: FRANCE: Berisha confident but disarmament will take time.
newsitem.headline: Berisha confident but disarmament will take time.

text.p: Albanian President Sali Berisha said in an interview published on Monday that his country was slowly returning to order but the recovery of looted weapons would take time.

"Order is being progressively re-established. There is a slight improvement but the disarming process cannot be swift," he told the French newspaper Le Monde in an interview conducted in Tirana on Saturday.
"There is a very special relationship between Albanians and their rifles. We are a warlike country and one has to be patient," he said.
The government has lost control of much of the country and local committees run many major towns. Lawlessness is however reported to be rife because of the activities of armed gangs.
"The disarmament process cannot be carried out by force except where gangs are involved. Another solution will have to be found for the population," he said.

The Albanian leader, whose country is teetering on the brink of civil war, denied he was faced with a popular uprising, describing those who sought to topple him as "bandits and rebels who absolutely do not represent the population."

"There is no reason to take into account the demands of dishonest people who loot banks and arms depots. Those groups are made up of former Stalinists, agents of the former Communist secret police, traffickers and the mafia. They are terrorising the population," he said.
Berisha also denied authoritarianism, saying he would resign if the opposition won elections in June.

He praised the role of the European Union, and particularly that of France, in seeking to aid his country. He also said he sought to improve ties with the United States, which had indicated it was not opposed to his resignation.

The EU has turned down an Albanian request for large-scale military intervention to help end the disorder in the country, sparked by popular anger over failed savings schemes that bankrupted thousands.
